item.title: [infoq] 一份数据，多种用途：Spotify 用 RAP 打通分析与在线服务
item.description: Spotify has introduced Random Access Parquet (RAP), a storage architecture that adds an external index to Apache Parquet files so key-based point queries can run directly on a data lake without copying data to an operational store. The same dataset can then serve analytics, machine learning, AI agents, and low-latency online features. RAP works with Iceberg tables and includes layout optimizations like sorting and covering indexes to cut query overhead.

item.title: [hackernews] Tracking down the 16-year-old WAL-reset SQLite bug
item.description: Tailscale and SQLite developers traced repeated, hard-to-explain corruption incidents to a 16-year-old WAL-Reset data race in SQLite, then found a second bug involving stale expression indexes. The investigation demonstrates how a race condition can hide in heavily used database code for more than a decade. It is a useful case study for anyone debugging concurrency or maintaining SQLite-backed systems.

item.description: An open-source GitHub project, mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills, provides 817 structured cybersecurity skills for AI agents across 29 security domains, mapped to six frameworks: MITRE ATT&CK, NIST CSF 2.0, MITRE ATLAS, D3FEND, NIST AI RMF, and MITRE F3. item.title: [github_trending] santifer/career-ops
item.description: career-ops is an open-source multi-agent job search system that scans job portals, scores listings with a structured A-F rubric normalized to 1.0-5.0, tailors CVs, and tracks applications — all locally inside an AI coding CLI such as Claude Code. It was built by someone frustrated with manual applications, giving candidates an AI-powered way to evaluate companies rather than just being filtered. Job seekers who work in the terminal may find it a practical fit.
